'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Pokrovsk offensive]]
***[[Russia]] formally claims control of [[Novohrodivka]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], twelve kilometers (seven miles) from the strategically important [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Logistics|logistical hub]] city [[Pokrovsk, Ukraine|Pokrovsk]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-troops-take-novohrodivka-ukraines-donetsk-region-ria-reports-2024-09-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Fall of Kabul (2021)|Fall of Kabul]], [[2020–2021 U.S. troop withdrawal from Afghanistan]]
***[[Republican Party (United States)|Republicans]] in the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] [[United States House Committee on Foreign Affairs|Foreign Affairs Committee]] release a report criticizing [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] for his handling of the withdrawal of [[United States Armed Forces|American forces]] from [[Afghanistan]]. [https://thehill.com/homenews/house/4868649-gop-report-afghanistan-withdrawal/ (''The Hill'')]
*[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**The [[Israeli military]] says that several [[Hezbollah]] militants were killed in [[airstrike]]s on Hezbollah targets in [[southern Lebanon|southern]] [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/9/8/israel-war-on-gaza-live-israel-kills-31-in-gaza-as-750000-march-in-israel (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Israel]] launches several airstrikes in central [[Syria]], targeting the [[Tartus Governorate|Tartus]] and [[Hama Governorate|Hama]] governorates. [https://edition.cnn.com/2024/09/08/middleeast/israeli-airstrikes-syria-intl-latam/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**The [[World Health Organization]] reports that the death toll from the [[civil war]] in [[Sudan]] has increased to more than 20,000 people. [https://apnews.com/article/sudan-military-rsf-war-f885e161c4eb4151377c25a20929de25 (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[76th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards]]
**[[United States|American]] [[historical drama]] television series ''[[Shōgun (2024 TV series)|Shōgun]]'' wins a record 14 [[Emmys]] at the 2024 [[Creative Arts Emmy Awards]], the most won for any single season. [https://apnews.com/article/emmys-shogun-creative-arts-jamie-lee-curtis-641b33fcad195467a39df91ce673d32f (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Wildfires in the United States during 2024]]
**Over 11,000 people are [[Emergency evacuation|evacuated]] in [[San Bernardino County, California|San Bernardino County]], [[California]], [[United States]], as the [[Line Fire]] quadruples in size to over {{conv|27|mi2|acre|abbr=on}}. [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/08/us/line-fire-san-bernardino-california.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvg5d69qlv0o (BBC News)]
*Forty-eight people and 50 [[cattle]] are killed in an [[explosion]] caused by a collision between a [[Tank truck|fuel tanker]] and a truck in [[Agaie]], [[Niger State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://apnews.com/article/nigeria-fuel-truck-collision-e082a840da51f7078dc2a54aed09ea92 (AP)]
*Fourteen people are killed and another person is injured when a [[bus crash]]es on a highway between [[Aden]] and [[Taiz]] in [[Yemen]].  [https://apnews.com/article/yemen-road-crash-civil-war-3613b87527a3130ade87ced508c215d6 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 Allenby Bridge shooting]]
**Three [[Israelis|Israeli]] [[civilian]]s are killed in a shooting at the [[Allenby Bridge]] on the Israel–[[Jordan]] border. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/two-wounded-shooting-attack-near-jordan-border-israeli-authorities-say-2024-09-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Kingdom of Jesus Christ compound standoff]]
**[[Kingdom of Jesus Christ (church)|Kingdom of Jesus Christ]] pastor [[Apollo Quiboloy]], who is charged with [[Sex trafficking in the Philippines|sex trafficking]], is arrested amid a standoff between the police and members of the church at the church's [[headquarters]] in [[Davao City]], [[Philippines]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/9/8/philippine-authorities-arrest-church-leader-charged-with-sex-trafficking (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2024 Pasaquina Bell UH-1 crash]]
**Nine people, including [[El Salvador]]'s [[National Civil Police (El Salvador)|National Civil Police]] chief [[Mauricio Arriaza Chicas]] and a fraud suspect, are killed during a helicopter crash while en route to [[San Salvador]]. The crash is considered to be intentional. All flags on government buildings will be flown [[half-mast]] for three days. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cz9w81plz3lo (BBC)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Algerian presidential election]]
**Incumbent [[President of Algeria]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]] is re-elected for his second term with 95% of the vote. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/9/8/algerias-abdelmadjid-tebboune-re-elected-president-with-94-7-percent-vote (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2024 Venezuelan political crisis]]
**[[Venezuelan opposition]] leader [[Edmundo González]] flees [[Venezuela]] to seek [[right of asylum|political asylum]] in [[Spain]]. The [[Government of Spain|Spanish government]] says that González left Venezuela on a [[Spanish Air and Space Force|Spanish Air Force]] plane at his own request. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c14zdypxr7no (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2024 Summer Paralympics]]
**[[Thailand at the 2024 Summer Paralympics]], [[Wheelchair fencing at the Summer Paralympics]]
***[[Thailand|Thai]] [[wheelchair fencer]] [[Saysunee Jana]] becomes the first female wheelchair fencer, and the second overall, to win gold medals in all three [[fencing]] disciplines, [[épée]], [[foil (fencing)|foil]], and [[sabre (fencing)|sabre]]. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/sports/2861203/saysunee-makes-history-with-paralympics-fencing-treble (''Bangkok Post'')]
*[[2024 US Open (tennis)|2024 US Open]]
**In [[tennis]], [[Jannik Sinner]] defeats [[Taylor Fritz]] in the final of the [[US Open (tennis)|US Open]] [[2024 US Open – Men's singles|Men's singles]] tournament to win his first US Open title ever and his second [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Tournaments|Grand Slam]] title overall. Sinner is also the first [[Italy|Italian]] man to ever win the US Open. [https://www.cnn.com/2024/09/08/sport/us-open-mens-final-sinner-fritz-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
